bull.b: The secured long-term PPA provides a foundation for Phase 1 development and reduces uncertainty around power availability, a critical requirement for data-center operations. It also supports customer discussions and gives the project a clearer path toward its targeted 2027 service start.

Full Phase 1 permitting and active site work indicate that the project has moved beyond early conceptual development into execution. Progress on clearing, grading, and remediation can improve delivery visibility and help convert the planned power capacity into operating infrastructure.

The reported cash position and remaining financing option provide resources to advance development and support leasing activity. This funding base may improve flexibility while the company finalizes project arrangements, although access to additional financing remains conditional on lease execution.

bear.b: The collapse in trailing revenue and deeply negative profitability show that the current operating base is not yet generating a stable, scalable business. Negative gross profit and widening losses could persistently limit internal funding capacity until development projects begin producing revenue.

Persistent operating cash outflows and negative free cash flow mean the company is consuming capital rather than funding operations internally. Continued development spending therefore increases reliance on equity, debt, or project financing and can constrain financial flexibility over the medium term.

The project’s conversion from power and site progress into contracted operating infrastructure still depends on completing the definitive lease. Until technical scope, payment timing, and delivery responsibilities are settled, development funding and the expected project timeline remain execution-dependent.
